thread:
Carlos: Heads-up — during the private customer hardening run we found a pod that had outbound egress to S3 enabled from an airgapped tenant namespace. :rotating_light:
Maya: :eyes: which tenant/env?
Carlos: tenant-42 in the staging VPC. This was during an image rebuild, container used an old base image that had a leftover AWS SDK config.
Omar: OK — immediate questions: 1) any KMS keys exposed? 2) RBAC change that allowed that pod to mount service account tokens?
Carlos: No key material in the image, but the pod had access to a mounted secret with a short-lived service token that allowed s3:PutObject. RBAC binding was a ClusterRole accidentally applied to the tenant namespace on deploy.
Nia: Steps: revoke the short-lived token, rotate the credential provider, and ensure netpol denies egress by default.
Devon: Agreed. I've started a rotate for the service principal and generated a new envelope key for tenant-42. security-bot: action:rotate_key tenant=tenant-42 id=enc-9f2 -> in progress.
oncall-ops: Re-deploying workloads with immutable tags now. Please confirm images pinned to digest.
Maya: For the netpol change, proposed minimal deny-everything then allow intra-namespace and required egress-proxy:
Maya: ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-external-egress
  namespace: tenant-42
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: egress-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 3128
```
Carlos: Good. Also need to add a validating admission rule to block ClusterRole bindings in tenant namespaces unless explicitly approved.
Omar: That's a policy we should codify in gatekeeper. Suggest constraint: deny clusterrolebinding where subject.namespace != "" and namespace matches tenant-.* and annotation not set.
Nia: For KMS: tenant requested dedicated envelope keys; we need to update docs about customer-managed keys vs platform-managed. For now, we generated enc-9f2 but recommend per-tenant CMKs in KMS + HSM for prod.
Devon: Post-mitigation checklist I propose: revoke token, rotate keys, apply netpol, apply gatekeeper constraint, run image-scan across tenant images, produce an audit log entry and page customers if any data exfil.
Carlos: On audit logging — we have kube-audit forwarding to the private SIEM but the S3 access appears to have been performed via SDK from pod. We captured pod logs and network flow logs but need to add object-level S3 audit (server access logs) to correlate.
Maya: Forensics: snapshot the node, collect container FS, and preserve policy for legal. Omar will kick off kubelet log collection.
Omar: Running `./tools/collect-forensics --node node-7 --namespace tenant-42` now.
security-bot: incident:forensics_collected tenant=tenant-42 node=node-7 artifact=/artifacts/2231122334/ -> done.
Nia: Vulnerability triage: base image had CVE-2024-XXXXX in curl. We'll need to block that tag and rebuild with patched base. Add CVE to tracking board and mark severity medium-high.
Devon: Communication plan: internal incident slack thread + security incident report template. If customer-data was touched, ops to prepare statement.
Carlos: Short-term mitigation is live. Long-term: (1) default-deny egress at cluster level for all private deployments, (2) mandatory per-tenant KMS isolation option, (3) gatekeeper constraint for RBAC changes, (4) automated image provenance checks pre-deploy.
Maya: I'll open the GH PR for netpol + gatekeeper constraint. Omar can add the image-scan job to CI.
Omar: Will do. Also recommend nightly audit queries to detect any pod creating AWS clients (heuristic: look for aws-sdk env or creds mounted).
Nia: Add a regression alert to Redwood Console: sudden uptick in external egress from private namespaces.
Devon: Good catch Carlos — thanks. Filing this as a drill -> we'll convert to an incident if we find customer data touched.
Carlos: Thanks all. I'll draft the incident notes and assign owners for the checklist items. :thumbsup:
